newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former Riviera political boss goes on trial.
newsitem.headline: Former Riviera political boss goes on trial.

text.p: A former Riviera political boss who liked to call himself "the Godfather" went on trial on Monday denying charges he took kickbacks in the latest political sleaze scandal in France.

Maurice Arreckx, 79, the representative of the southern Var department to the French senate when arrested in August 1994, is alleged to have extorted 1.8 million francs ($350,000) in return for a construction contract in Toulon, south France, in 1991.

Arreckx, the first defendant to take the stand in the Toulon court, denied the charges and argued that the purchase of the land for a planned engineering college had been decided by Toulon's administration rather than by him personally.

"It was not I who chose the plot of land, it was the city of Toulon," Arreckx, dressed in a blue suit, said at the start of the trial which is expected to last a week. Arreckx was mayor of the Mediterranean port city for 26 years until 1985.
But a lawyer for the city, Andre Gas, argued that Toulon had paid 3.5 million francs ($690,000) too much for the land.
"To corrupt someone, you need money. The price of the plot went up 3.5 million francs in 10 days. That means 3.5 million francs less in the taxpayers' pockets," Gas said.
The lawyer urged that the city be allowed to run a civil action in the court against Arreckx in parallel with the state's criminal action.

But the court deferred action on the request when lawyers for Arreckx and his five co-defendants argued that Toulon, now governed by the extreme-right National Front, would use the trial as a forum to attack the former administration, the centre-right Union for French Democracy (UDF).
The trial could expose shadowy ties between politicians, companies and the underworld along the Cote d'Azur, where numerous politicians have been involved in corruption probes.
The Arreckx case has drawn special attention because of his reputed ties with local gangland chief Jean-Louis Fargette who has since been murdered.
Investigators have said that Fargette claimed that Arreckx "swindled" him out of a cut in the kickback money, which was alleged to have been paid by a unit of utilities group Cie Generale des Eaux.

The Var has been under the spotlight since 1993 when local parliamentarian Yann Piat, like Arreckx a member of the UDF, was killed after she threatened to reveal "Mafia-like" activities in the region.
Arreckx, who could be imprisoned for up to 10 years if convicted, has already spent 288 days in jail in pre-trial detention.

He was conditionally released from jail for health reasons in May 1995 pending trial. He initially claimed the funds he partly received in a Swiss bank account were for his UDF party which he claimed had "sacrificed" him.
"I am a man of private means," he responded at the trial's start when asked his profession.

Another top southern politician, Cannes mayor Michel Mouillot, is in detention on suspicion of extorting cash from a British casino. And mayors of Nice, Lyon and Grenoble have all been embroiled in political scandals.
